data.narrative:
Electric Air, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Chris Mui and Jeremy Osbourne, has raised $500K to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine Climate & Energy peers: one public company (Lnza) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A Peer-Median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient datapoints at the same or adjacent stage within a comparable valuation tier; only three or more peers meeting narrow filters would support this method. Consequently, the analysis relies on Stage-Progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $500K total raised proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $1.25M.

The triangulated range is $1.06M to $1.44M (low to high), with a median of $1.25M, derived from a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for Electric Air's specific risk profile and the absence of direct peer multiples at this early stage. A subsequent valuation should incorporate additional datapoints as comparable seed-stage transactions in climate tech become available or as Electric Air's technical progress and market traction become clearer.
